newsitem.title: MEXICO: INSIGHT - Vitro notes help debt but cost high.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Vitro notes help debt but cost high.

text.p: Medium-term notes issued by glassmaker Vitro, S.A. will help refinance the company's short-term debt but analysts said on Tuesday they had reservations over the high fixed rate offered.
Vitro offered 515 million pesos of medium-term notes on Monday, which are denominated in inflation-indexed UDIs, fall due on December 7, 1999 and offer a fixed real interest rate of 13 percent.
The offer is worth approximately 305.86 million UDIs, an inflation indexed unit of investment, and expires on Tuesday.

"As a rating agency, the most important thing for us is cash flow," said Aurelio Cavazos, an analyst at Duff and Phelps (DCR). "In our analysis, we see that Vitro has the capacity and cash flow to meet its obligations."
DCR rated the notes at MAA-, which places it among high-quality credits.
"The most immediate benefit of the offer is liquidity for the holding company, as there are only 13 payments to be made every 84 days," Vitro's financing manager Patricio Coindreau told Reuters.
"Previously payments were made every 14 or 28 days. We managed to reduce short-term debt, especially in commercial paper," Coindreau added.
Coindreau said that 92 percent of Vitro's debt at the holding-company level was long-term, the rest being short-term.
A real rate of 13 percent was equivalent to Mexico's TIIE interbank rate plus 200 basis points, or "very close to current market rates."

"Refinancing debt is good, but the commitment to pay 13 percent real interest over three years is high, independent of Vitro's company risk," said Sandra Morfin, an equity analyst at Caspian Research.
Sergio Torres, of Inverlat International, said "a rate of 13 percent on UDIs is very attractive to a buyer, when average real rates are eight percent for 1996, and maybe seven percent in 1997."
"The most important point is that Vitro made a commitment to reduce the cost of its debt. My first impression is that this offer does not help to achieve that aim," Torres added.
